item.title: BZE Status Update — Oct 23, 2026
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
Two weeks ago we closed with “test v8.2.0 on testnet, then bring it to mainnet”. That is where we are: v8.2.0 is released, the upgrade proposal has passed, and the mainnet upgrade is days away. Meanwhile the BZE Explorer went live, you can vote on proposals from the Staking app, and the testnet apps got a new look and a rebuilt Factory.

v8.2.0: Mainnet Upgrade Approved

After two weeks on testnet, BZE v8.2.0 was released on October 14, and governance approved the upgrade without a single vote against. It activates at block height 25,263,600, which at the current pace lands around October 26. Validators: please build the new version with Go 1.26 and be ready for the height.

What v8.2.0 brings was covered last time: Denom Rewards, where any token gets its own staking pool paying out in up to 50 tokens, on-chain token branding, tighter reward math, and a round of fixes. The apps are adapted on testnet and move to mainnet right after the upgrade: reward pools and brand kits in the Factory, staking and one-click claiming on the DEX. The promised Denom Rewards article will be published with the upgrade.

A reminder on Noble USDC. From the upgrade height, BZE stops accepting new USDC from Noble — only the income transfers, you will always be able to withdraw. What you already hold keeps working: you can still trade it, send it and withdraw it to Noble. Circle has stopped minting USDC on Noble and the exit limits start shrinking from October 31, so if you hold USDC.n on BZE, please move it now. If some is in a liquidity pool, remove your liquidity first. A step-by-step guide follows this update.

The BZE Explorer Is Live

Two updates ago it was a plan. Today the explorer is live at explorer.getbze.com, with the full history of the chain from block one, and the testnet has its own at testnet-explorer.getbze.com.

It is an explorer that understands BZE. Every transaction is explained in plain words, with where the funds went. DEX orders are followed from placement to fill, and things that happen without a transaction, like order fills, reward payouts, burns and raffles, show up where they belong. Validators have their uptime, stake changes and a Hall of Fame for the ones that vote. The apps now link to it, and old explorer links keep working. A dedicated tour follows this update.

Vote From the Staking App

Governance moved into the Staking app. staking.getbze.com lists every proposal with its tally, how the validators voted and your own voting power, and lets you vote with your wallet. When a proposal is open, a badge in the navigation and a banner on your dashboard make sure you don’t miss it. The v8.2.0 proposal was the first one many of you voted on this way.

Also on the mainnet apps: an Apps menu with the new app icons, slippage shown in the DEX swap summary, fixes to swap amounts and USD values, and no more getting stuck on “Keplr not installed”.

On Testnet: A New Look and a New Factory

The five web apps on testnet share a new design: light and dark mode, the same header, wallet and settings drawers everywhere, each app in its own colour. It goes to mainnet after v8.2.0.

The Factory was rebuilt around what you want to do rather than which chain feature does it. You start from a goal: create a token, make it tradable, reward your holders, send it to a list of wallets, run a burning raffle, or get your logo into every wallet through the Cosmos chain registry. Each is a short guided wizard with a review step and a “Done” screen that suggests the next move. Rewards have plain names now: a Simple reward pays a fixed prize over a fixed term, a Compounded reward is your token’s own pool with daily prizes and airdrops.

Communities, also on testnet, became what we described last time: every token’s page is the project’s own site, in its colours and font, where holders stake, earn, trade, burn and join the raffle without ever learning about BeeZee.

Try it at testnet-factory.getbze.com, testnet-dex.getbze.com and testnet-communities.getbze.com. docs.getbze.com was updated along the way.

Looking Further Ahead

Work on v8.3.0 has started. It updates the chain’s core libraries to this year’s releases with their security fixes, lets governance assign a new admin to a renounced token and adjust the fees of existing liquidity pools, lets a token’s admin lock minting for good, and fixes a few things found while writing the tests.

It also brings DAOs. Last time we said the DAO module was postponed in favour of DAO DAO contracts. Since CosmWasm still has no date, communities should not wait for it: v8.3.0 includes a native DAO module, where a DAO is run by a fixed member list or by the stakers of a token’s reward pools, with proposals, voting and a treasury. More when it reaches testnet.

What Comes Next

The mainnet upgrade to v8.2.0, then the mainnet apps catch up with testnet: Denom Rewards, token branding, the new look, the new Factory and Communities. Then v8.3.0 goes to testnet.

Thank you to everyone who voted, tested and asked questions.

BZE keeps moving forward.

item.title: BZE Status Update — Oct 8, 2026
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
It has been a while since our last update. The summer was quiet but development kept going: a mainnet patch release, a new chain version now live on testnet, a new app for creators, the start of our own block explorer, and one change we didn’t see coming around USDC. Some things we mentioned earlier are taking longer than planned, and we explain why below.

v8.1.1 on Mainnet, v8.2.0 in Testing

In early July, mainnet upgraded to v8.1.1 at block height 23,855,000. It was small, but it fixed pool creation for token pairs with very long names.

Most of the chain work since then went into v8.2.0, which is now live on testnet. Its main new feature is Denom Rewards. Any token on BZE can have its own staking pool, and that pool can pay stakers in any token, up to 50 different tokens at a time. Anyone can fund it, either as a daily payout campaign or as a one-time airdrop. A project can reward its holders in BZE, a stablecoin, or a partner’s token, and stakers claim everything in one transaction. A dedicated article will follow with the full details.

Under the hood, v8.2.0 also lays safer foundations: a round of bug fixes, the latest CometBFT patches, tighter reward math, the option for anyone to clean up finished rewards, and an extra round of funds-safety testing.

A note on Noble USDC

Circle is retiring USDC on the Noble chain, and the USDC that came to BZE from Noble loses its backing in January 2027. This was never part of our roadmap. The wind-down came much sooner than anyone expected, so we adjusted our plans and made room for it in v8.2.0, because keeping BZE users and the DEX safe comes first. Once it reaches mainnet, v8.2.0 stops accepting new USDC from Noble. The protocol-owned USDC/BZE liquidity will move to USDC issued on Injective. Governance can also pause trading of a token that loses its backing, while withdrawals, cancellations and transfers keep working. A dedicated article will follow with the full migration details.

If you hold Noble USDC on BZE, please don’t wait for it: start moving your USDC out now. If some of it is in a liquidity pool, remove your liquidity first. Sending USDC from BZE back to Noble works today and will stay open, but the sooner you do it, the safer you are.

More details about it:

  • Circle is Discontinuing Support for USDC and CCTP V1 on Noble (Circle blog)
  • Circle Is Leaving Cosmos Behind (Forkast)
  • Circle Discontinues USDC Support on Noble Blockchain, Ends CCTP V1 (KuCoin News)

What happened to CosmWasm and the DAO module?

In earlier updates we said the next release would bring CosmWasm smart contracts and a native DAO module. Neither is in v8.2.0, and we want to be open about why.

CosmWasm is delayed on purpose. Adding smart contracts opens a whole new surface on a chain whose code was just audited. We don’t want to open the door to new bugs or new exploits, so we are taking it one careful step at a time. For now its timing is uncertain, and we would rather say so than promise a date.

The DAO module is postponed for a different reason. Our feedback suggests that if BZE gets CosmWasm, communities would rather use DAO DAO, the widely used DAO smart contracts, than a separate native module. So it makes more sense to build on that path than to maintain two ways of doing the same thing.

Token Branding: Giving Every Token Its Own Identity

v8.2.0 also brings on-chain token branding, and it is the first step toward something bigger.

With v8.2.0, the admin of a token created on BZE can store the token’s own look directly on the chain: a font, plus color palettes for light and dark mode. Because it lives on the chain and not on one website, every app that shows the token can use the same identity, exactly as its creators designed it.

This is the foundation for what comes next. The upcoming Communities app will give every token its own page, shown in that token’s colors, and more tools for communities will build on the same branding. Until now, tokens on BZE all looked alike. With branding, each project can start building a recognizable identity on our chain.

Introducing the Factory App

We mentioned it before as “coming soon”, and now it’s official: the Factory app is live at factory.getbze.com. It has been quietly online for a while, as we wanted to test it properly before announcing it.

Factory is the home for creators and projects on BZE, with every creator tool in one place:

  • Create a token with its supply, name, logo and admin settings in one guided flow.
  • Open a market on the DEX for any pair of assets.
  • Create a liquidity pool, set its swap fee and decide where the fees go, or add liquidity to an existing one.
  • Set up a staking reward so your community can stake a token and earn your prize.
  • Manage your creations in one place: supply, admin status and everything you launched.

Thinking about launching a token on BZE? This is the easiest way to start, and more tools will follow as new chain features go live.

DEX and the Web Apps

The DEX got a set of everyday improvements:

  • Trading fees are now shown in the fee token you picked, not only in BZE.
  • MAX buttons and balance checks now leave room for the network fee, so you no longer hit “insufficient funds” by a tiny amount.
  • A new asset details page shows the key facts about each token.

Behind the scenes, every app now has automated tests, we made reliability and infrastructure improvements, and the price data behind the DEX, getbze.com and CoinGecko loads faster.

A Block Explorer Built for BZE

Work has started on a block explorer built specifically for BZE. As the chain grows, generic explorers can’t keep up. They only show raw transactions and don’t understand what BZE’s DEX, burner, rewards and tokens actually do.

Our explorer will, and it will be a natural addition to all our other tools: a place where anyone can see, openly and transparently, how the chain works and where funds are sent. We want it to be easy for anyone on their first visit, with a familiar layout for people coming from other ecosystems and plain-language explanations of what each transaction actually did. It is being built to grow along with the chain, so new features show up there properly from day one.

Also in Development

  • BZE Hub, our desktop app that runs its own node so you can use BZE even when public endpoints are down, already covers the portfolio, send and receive, swaps, a full trading terminal and liquidity pools. Staking and earning come next.
  • Communities, a branded page for every token created on BZE, is also on the way.

What Comes Next

The immediate focus is adapting our apps to the new features, testing v8.2.0 on testnet and then bringing it to mainnet. The upgrade height will be announced separately.

Thank you to everyone who keeps testing, trading, building and asking questions.

BZE keeps moving forward.

item.title: BZE Code Audited by Oak Security
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
Security is important for BZE. Not just because it sounds good, but because the network needs to be safe, stable, and ready for long-term use. That is why we are happy to share that the BZE code has been audited by Oak Security.

The audit was done in two phases, and both reports are public here. We will not go too deep into technical details in this article. The reports are there for anyone who wants to read them.

The most important thing to know is this: The current BZE mainnet already includes the fixes from the audit. So the network running today is already using the audited and fixed code.

Keeping the audited code stable

After an audit, one of the most important things is not to keep changing the same code over and over again without a very good reason. That is why the audited code will stay as it is as much as possible. We will only modify it when it is really needed. Of course, BZE will continue to grow. But we want to do that in a careful way, without making unnecessary changes to parts of the code that are already reviewed and running on mainnet.

What comes next

The next BZE release will bring an important new feature: CosmWasm smart contracts. This means builders will be able to create and launch smart contracts directly in the BZE ecosystem. For the community, this is a big step. It opens the door for more tools, more apps, and more use cases to be built on top of BZE. We see this as one of the next important parts of the project. The base network is running, the audited fixes are already live, and now we can start opening more space for builders.

How other projects can use BZE Network

BZE Network is not only for BZE. Any project can use the chain almost like it is their own network. This can be a project issued directly on BZE, or a project from another chain connected through IBC. The main condition is simple: the project needs to have a strong liquidity pool with its token paired with BZE.

With that in place, the project can build its own UI on top of the BZE blockchain and let its users interact using only that project’s token. Users do not need to care about BZE, fees, swaps, or what happens in the background. They just use the app with the token they already know.

Behind the scenes, the project gets to use the features of a working network, with audited code already running on mainnet. And with CosmWasm smart contracts coming in the next release, projects will have even more flexibility. They will be able to build custom features, automate flows, and create more advanced tools around their own token and community.

This opens the door for other teams to build on BZE without having to launch and maintain their own chain. They can focus on their product, their users, and their token, while BZE provides the base layer.

A step forward for BZE

This audit is not the end of the work. It is another step in making BZE stronger and better prepared for what comes next. We want BZE to be a network that people can use, build on, and trust. That takes time. It also takes boring work sometimes: reviews, fixes, testing, and careful releases.

But this is the kind of work that matters. Thanks to Oak Security for the audit, and thanks to everyone in the BZE community who keeps supporting the project.

BZE keeps moving forward.

item.title: BZE Status Update — May 2, 2026
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
BeeZee v8.1.0 Is Live on Mainnet

The biggest milestone since our previous status update is now official: BZE Blockchain v8.1.0 is live on mainnet.

The upgrade activated at block height 22,551,810, with the activation timestamp recorded at April 28, 2026, 15:52:25 UTC. This marks the completion of the upgrade path discussed in our March update and opens the door for the next phase of ecosystem improvements built around more flexible fee handling, better dApp usability, and stronger infrastructure for builders.

v8.1.0 is also the version that went through the recent audit process. We will cover the audit itself separately, in a dedicated article, so this update will stay focused on what the upgrade now enables for the BZE ecosystem.

Beyond the visible feature improvements, v8.1.0 also introduces a series of internal hardening changes designed to make the chain more predictable, resilient, and easier to operate safely. Several background processes now have clearer execution limits and safer processing flows, reducing the risk of heavy operations affecting block performance. The release also brings improvements to fee flows, DEX behavior, and general chain maintenance. These changes may not be immediately visible to everyday users, but they are important for keeping the network stable as activity grows.

Using BZE dApps Without Holding BZE

One of the most practical improvements introduced by v8.1.0 is that users are no longer required to hold native BZE coins directly in order to interact with BZE-powered applications.

Transaction fees can now be paid using supported assets such as PHOTON, USDC, and VDL. These assets are currently eligible because they have liquidity pools paired with BZE, and those pools contain more than the required amount of BZE liquidity.

In practice, this means a user can open a BZE dApp, select their preferred fee token in the application settings, and use the blockchain without first needing to acquire BZE for gas. A PHOTON holder, a USDC holder, or a VDL holder can interact with BZE applications using the asset they already have.

Fee-token eligibility is automatic and liquidity-based. Any asset that creates a liquidity pool with BZE can become eligible for fee payments once the BZE side of that pool reaches the required threshold. This threshold is controlled by governance through the TradeBin module parameter minNativeLiquidityForModuleSwap, which is currently set to 100,000 BZE.

If a pool later falls below that amount, the asset will no longer be available as a fee token until the liquidity requirement is met again.

This approach lowers onboarding friction while still keeping BZE at the economic foundation of the network. The chain can calculate fair fee values using BZE liquidity in the background, while users and applications get more flexibility at the front end.

v8.1.0 also improves how minimum gas fees are handled across the network. Until now, minimum gas prices were mainly controlled through each validator’s local node configuration, which meant fee requirements could vary from one validator to another. With this upgrade, the transaction fee collector module introduces a network-level minimum validator gas fee parameter.

Validators can still configure their own local minimums, but when the native BZE fee denomination is used, the effective minimum cannot go below the value defined by the module. Validators may still require a higher fee locally, but the module now provides a shared baseline for the network.

For example, assume the network-level minimum is 0.01 ubze per gas unit. If a validator sets its local native minimum below that value, the module-defined minimum is used instead. If a validator sets a higher local native minimum, the validator’s higher value is used. In other words, the module parameter acts as a floor, not as a fixed fee for every validator.

The same principle applies when a transaction pays fees in another supported denomination. For example, assume a transaction pays fees in PHOTON. If the on-chain pool price is 1 PHOTON = 70 BZE, then the PHOTON fee requirement is calculated from the BZE-equivalent value of the native minimum.

Because 1 BZE = 1,000,000 ubze, a minimum of 0.01 ubze equals 0.00000001 BZE. At a price of 1 PHOTON = 70 BZE, that translates to approximately 0.000000000142857 PHOTON per gas unit, before comparing it with any validator-local PHOTON minimum. If the validator’s local PHOTON minimum is higher, the higher value is used.

This creates a more flexible fee system without weakening the economic baseline of the network. Users and applications can pay transaction fees using supported ecosystem assets, while validators and the chain continue to rely on a minimum value anchored to BZE liquidity.

It is an important step toward making BZE more practical for token-based applications, IBC assets, and future payment flows.

What We’re Building Next

While v8.1.0 is now live, development has not slowed down. Several major pieces are already being worked on behind the scenes, all aimed at making BZE easier to build on, easier to use, and more resilient as an ecosystem.

The next major protocol upgrade is already in progress. This upgrade is planned to bring CosmWasm smart contracts to BZE, opening the door for a much wider range of decentralized applications and programmable on-chain logic.

Alongside CosmWasm, next version is also expected to introduce a dedicated DAO module. This module will be inspired by the functionality of DAO DAO smart contracts, but built as a native BZE module for communities that want to create and manage their own DAOs directly on the BZE network.

Another important project currently in development is BZE Hub, a desktop application designed to let users interact with the blockchain through a light local node. This matters because it reduces dependence on centralized API endpoints. If public endpoints are unavailable or overloaded, users should still have a way to interact with the blockchain locally. BZE Hub is part of our broader effort to strengthen decentralization not only at the validator level, but also at the user-access level.

We are also working on the Factory App, which will become an important interface for creators and projects building on BZE. The Factory App is intended to make it easier to create tokens, markets, staking programs, and other ecosystem components without needing to interact directly with low-level blockchain commands.

In addition to these, there are other features being worked on that will be disclosed at the right time.

Supporting AtomOne Liquidity Through BZE Community Validator

We also want to invite ATONE stakers to consider delegating to the BZE Community validator on AtomOne.

For ATONE holders, this is a simple way to support the broader ecosystem without changing their exposure: they continue staking ATONE while helping strengthen the connection between AtomOne and BZE.

The validator commission is not treated as profit. It is used for ecosystem-focused actions, including supporting liquidity for ATONE and PHOTON, AtomOne’s fee token, on BeeZee Blockchain.

Part of this process also involves burning ATONE to mint PHOTON, contributing to ATONE deflation while helping PHOTON become more useful across ecosystems. As PHOTON liquidity grows on BeeZee Blockchain, PHOTON can serve not only as AtomOne’s fee token, but also as a supported fee token for BZE dApps and transactions.

This is another example of how liquidity, utility, and cross-chain collaboration can work together. By supporting the BZE Community validator on AtomOne, ATONE stakers can help build deeper liquidity and stronger connections between both ecosystems.

Closing Thoughts

The activation of BZE Blockchain v8.1.0 is a major milestone for the network.

It makes the chain more flexible, improves the user experience for dApps, strengthens internal processing, and creates a practical path for supported assets such as PHOTON, USDC, and VDL to be used directly as fee tokens.

Most importantly, it moves BZE closer to a future where users can interact with blockchain applications in a simpler and more natural way. They should not have to think about every technical requirement in the background. They should be able to open an application, choose the asset they want to use, and start interacting.

v8.1.0 is an important step in that direction.

With the next version, CosmWasm, the DAO module, BZE Hub, Factory App, and other upcoming features already in progress, the foundation is being prepared for the next stage of BZE growth.

First time hearing about us? Visit our website to learn more about BZE.

item.title: BZE Status Update — Mar 19, 2026
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
A lot has been happening around BZE lately, even if not all of it was visible from the outside. This period brought progress on the upcoming v8.1.0 blockchain upgrade, important security work, and new steps forward for CoinTrunk as part of the wider BZE ecosystem.

Some planned roadmap items moved slower than expected, but that came with good reason. The work done during this cycle helps build a stronger base for what comes next and opens the door for new utility across the network.

BZE Blockchain v8.1.0

One of the main highlights of this update is the upcoming BZE Blockchain v8.1.0 upgrade. This release is focused on making the network more flexible, more efficient, and easier to build on, while also improving the overall foundation of the chain for future growth.

The biggest change is that tokens with liquidity paired against BZE will be able to do more than just cover normal transaction fees. With v8.1.0, they can also be used for other blockchain fees across the ecosystem, including things like market-related fees, creation fees, and other custom costs. This opens the door for projects building on BZE to offer access to their tools and services using their own token, which lowers friction for new users and makes the whole experience more accessible.

Beyond that, the upgrade also improves how fees, rewards, and liquidity-related operations are handled across the blockchain. It brings a stronger structure to core network processes, better precision in key areas, updated infrastructure and dependencies, and a more robust framework for supporting future expansion. Altogether, v8.1.0 is not just a technical update — it is an important step toward making BZE a more practical and developer-friendly blockchain.

The upgrade is currently in testing, with the new version already going through final validation before release. If everything continues as expected, v8.1.0 should be deployed on testnet during the following week, and shortly after on mainnet.

Security Audit

Another important focus during this period was the security audit. While it did slow down some of the roadmap items that were originally planned for this stage, it was a necessary step toward making the BZE blockchain more secure, more stable, and more prepared for long-term growth.

The audit also came with costs of several thousand dollars, making it one of the more meaningful investments in this phase of development. To recognize the support that helped make this possible, 10 million BZE from the community pool will be allocated as a reward to the sponsor who covered these costs. Under the agreement, those tokens will be staked for the agreed period, helping align that support with the long-term health of the network.

A dedicated article will follow shortly once the full audit report is published, covering the findings, the outcome of the process, and more details around this arrangement.

CoinTrunk Update

CoinTrunk also moved forward during this cycle, with a revamped website now live and a clearer direction for its role inside the wider BZE ecosystem. As a BZE sub-project, CoinTrunk continues to focus mainly on services built around BZE and Cosmos, while also leaving room for broader utility over time.

Work has also already started on a basic payment processor for BZE blockchain coins and tokens, a direction that is now reflected in the public roadmap. This is an important step in turning CoinTrunk into a more practical utility layer, with solutions that can connect blockchain use cases to real services and everyday access.

As an early real-world example of that direction, a small Web2 online business launched by Stefan’s company, is expected to become the first merchant to accept BZE as payment for its services. It is a small but meaningful starting point that makes this utility directly accessible to the BZE community and holders.

CoinTrunk Mobile App

At the same time, an important change was made regarding the CoinTrunk mobile app. Following its delisting from the Android app store due to administrative issues related to the developer account, work on the app has been stopped and mobile development under CoinTrunk is now postponed for an indefinite period.

That said, the wallet direction inside the ecosystem continues through Vidulum, a project built on the BZE blockchain. Vidulum is working on a more advanced solution tailored for BZE while also supporting other networks, with a broader approach across both browser and mobile environments.

Behind the Scenes

Another part of this cycle also went into launching a new testnet environment, an important step for ongoing development and validation. While it is not one of the main headlines of this update, it supported the broader progress happening across the ecosystem and took part in the work behind the scenes.

A special thanks also goes to ChainTools for being a valuable help on the infrastructure side and for their continued support.

Updated Roadmap and Ecosystem Links

The public roadmap on the BZE website has also been updated to reflect the latest direction and current progress across the ecosystem. It is the best place to follow what is being worked on, what has already moved forward, and what is planned next.

For anyone who wants to explore more, make sure to visit both the BZE website and CoinTrunk.io. Together, they offer the clearest view of how the ecosystem is growing, from blockchain development and roadmap progress to the practical products being built around it.

item.title: BZE Status Update — UI Evolution Begins
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
BZE Status Update — UI Evolution Begins

In our BZE Status Update — Nov 20, 2025 (Introducing the V8 Upgrade) article, we introduced the V8 Upgrade — a major leap forward for the BZE network. We’re happy to report that V8 is now running smoothly on mainnet, powering the next chapter of BeeZee’s development with Cosmos SDK 0.50 and new on-chain features like AMMs and multi-asset gas fees.

Now, it’s time to bring the user interface in line with those changes.

One App Becomes Three

As part of our UI overhaul, we’re breaking the original all-in-one BeeZee App into three focused dApps, each serving a specific purpose:

  • DEX App — for swaps, liquidity provision, and staking (coming soon)
  • Burner & Raffles App — for community burn events and burn raffles (live now https://burner.getbze.com 🔥)
  • Factory App — for token creation, upgrades, and future builder tools (coming soon)

This change was announced alongside V8, and we’re now starting to roll it out — beginning with the Burner App, which is already live and hosting its first burning raffle.

Why Split the UI?

The original BeeZee App served its purpose, but it tried to do too much in one place. By splitting the interface into dedicated apps, we can make each experience faster, cleaner, and easier to use.

It also helps us move faster — updates and new features can now be rolled out independently for each dApp, without affecting unrelated components. This modular approach reflects our broader vision for the BZE ecosystem: scalable, flexible, and future-ready.

Introducing the Wallet Sidebar

All new dApps will feature a powerful new tool: the BZE Wallet Sidebar — a built-in interface that lets users send any token across the BeeZee network and manage transactions more intuitively.

While we still rely on third-party wallets (like Keplr) to sign transactions, this sidebar eliminates a key limitation:
you no longer need to submit a pull request to Keplr just to use a new token.

With this upgrade, the blockchain itself handles multi-asset fee support — any token with deep enough liquidity against BZE can be used to pay gas fees, and the Wallet Sidebar lets users choose their preferred fee token easily.

This significantly lowers the barrier for new token creators and removes technical friction from launching and using tokens on the BeeZee network.

That’s it for now — more updates are on the way as we roll out the DEX and Factory apps. Until then, explore the new Burner App and let us know what you think!

item.title: BZE Status Update — Nov 20, 2025 (Introducing the V8 Upgrade)
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
BZE Status Update — Nov 20, 2025 (Introducing the V8 Upgrade)

We’re back with another major milestone for the BZE network. The long-awaited V8 Upgrade is officially happening — a powerful leap forward packed with essential improvements, new features, and a refreshed experience across the ecosystem.

While this upgrade arrives a bit later than originally planned, the delay comes with purpose: we chose to bundle more enhancements into one big release rather than spacing them out. That means more impact, fewer transitions, and a faster path to our long-term goals.

Key Features in This Release

Automated Market Makers (AMMs): BZE now supports Automated Market Makers — enabling anyone to create liquidity pools and swap tokens instantly. This sits alongside our existing order-book DEX, giving users the best of both worlds. Swap fees collected from AMM activity can be distributed among liquidity providers, the burner, and the community pool — depending on how each pool is configured. This gives pool creators greater control and supports both incentives and long-term sustainability.

Multi-Asset Transaction Fees: With this upgrade, users can now pay gas fees using tokens other than BZE. This makes BZE a more flexible and appealing platform for other token projects and everyday users alike.

Major Technical Leap: Cosmos SDK v0.50: This upgrade brings BZE straight to Cosmos SDK v0.50, skipping intermediate versions like 0.46 and 0.47. It brings improved performance and a more flexible codebase that allows us to build and iterate faster going forward.

What This Upgrade Unlocks

Beyond the features going live now, the V8 Upgrade lays the groundwork for future additions, including:

  • Tokens with built-in governance features
  • Minable tokens and dynamic supply mechanics
  • Community pools for token-specific initiatives
  • Tools for creators and builders to take their projects further on the BZE network

It’s not just about what’s changing today — it’s about what becomes possible next.

A Brand New App Experience: Introducing Three DApps

The V8 Upgrade also comes with a full UI overhaul, replacing the current single-app layout with a modular interface made of three dedicated DApps:

  1. DEX App — for trading, liquidity, and staking
  2. Burning & Raffles App — where users can view burn events, participate in community raffles, and support token burns (including from third-party tokens built on BZE)
  3. Factory App — a launchpad for builders and communities to create tokens, launch staking, and in the future, even deploy their own blockchain. While the initial version will be simple, we plan to expand it over time into a powerful toolkit for token and community creation.

The transition to these new dApps will happen gradually in the days following the upgrade. The current DApp will remain fully functional until the full switch is complete.

🔥 The Burn Continues

As always, sustainability remains at the heart of BZE. Swap fees continue to contribute to regular burn events, reducing supply and strengthening the long-term value of the ecosystem. Burning raffles — where users can contribute to be part of the event and win a portion of the pot — will also remain a key part of the community experience.

And with the new dedicated dApp for burn events, we’re making it easier than ever to take part — not just for BZE holders, but for any token issued on our chain.

🚀 V8 Upgrade Activates on Nov 27

The V8 Upgrade will go live at block height 20237800, expected to be reached on November 27, 2025.

At the upgrade height, the network will briefly pause to complete necessary migrations — a process that should take no more than a minute. Once complete, BZE mainnet will resume operations with all the new features in place.

The V8 Upgrade is a big step for the BZE ecosystem — and just the beginning of what’s coming next.

item.title: BZE Status Update May 4, 2025
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
It’s been a little while since our last update, and we’ve been hard at work behind the scenes. If you missed the previous status update, you can catch up here.

BZE Burnings

To help fight inflation and keep BZE sustainable long-term, we burn coins collected from trading fees every four weeks. This reduces the total supply over time and strengthens the value of the remaining tokens.

On top of that, we regularly host burning raffles. These events let community members voluntarily contribute BZE to be burned, and in return, they get a chance to win a percentage of the total pot. It’s a fun and impactful way to get involved in the ecosystem.

Since our last update, over 105,311 BZE have been burned. That brings the total burned amount to 180,539,229 BZE since the beginning of the project. And we’re just getting started — burnings will continue as BZE keeps growing.

Expanding the community

CoinTrunk new Publishers

We’re beginning to take the first steps toward evolving CoinTrunk, our module for publishing news and media directly on the BZE blockchain.

Recently, a new publisher, @CosmosBG, was added on-chain and has been doing a fantastic job sharing insightful chronicles through our decentralized platform.

Even more exciting — @CosmosEcosystem, a well-known contributor to Cosmos-related news, has agreed to become a publisher as well. At the time of writing, the governance proposal to officially add them is live and expected to pass in the next few days.

Building Partnerships

Since the beginning of the year, we’ve been actively curating partnerships and reaching out to other projects for listings and collaborations. BZE is steadily gaining trust in the space as a serious, long-term project — not a quick cash grab. If you’re building something of your own, we’re always open to exploring win-win partnerships.

Next Network Upgrade: A Big Leap Forward

We’ve been working hard behind the scenes on the next BZE network upgrade. While it’s arriving a bit later than originally scheduled, that delay comes with a good reason — we decided to pack more features into a single upgrade rather than rolling them out in separate stages. This approach allows us to reach bigger goals, faster.

The upgrade will jump directly to Cosmos SDK 0.50, skipping over intermediate versions like 0.46 and 0.47. This leap forward brings significant improvements, important security enhancements, and helps us move closer to our long-term goals at a faster pace.

One of the major features being introduced is Automated Market Makers (AMMs), which will let users create liquidity pools and perform instant token swaps. This will sit alongside our existing order-book DEX, giving users more flexibility and better trading experiences.

We’re also enabling multi-asset transaction fees, meaning users will be able to pay gas fees in tokens other than BZE. This is a big step toward making BZE’s blockchain more attractive for other projects looking to build on a reliable, scalable network.

All of these changes set the stage for new possibilities — more features, deeper integrations, and stronger partnerships.

item.title: BZE Status Update March 21, 2025
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
It’s been a while since our last status update — and we know many of you have been eager to hear what we’ve been working on. Truth is, we’ve had our heads down, focused on building and improving the BZE chain.

🚀 Network Upgrade v7.2.0: Better Trading, Easier Access, and Smarter Burning

One of the biggest milestones since our last update was the launch of network upgrade v7.2.0 — a release focused on making BZE faster, easier to use, and more efficient.

Here’s what changed:

  • Bulk Order Execution on the DEX
    Previously, executing multiple trades meant sending multiple transactions — each with its own fee. With v7.2.0, orders can now be executed in batches, which means fewer transactions and lower costs. You can now fill multiple orders in one go and pay just one trading fee and one transaction fee. It’s a smoother experience for everyone.
  • Ledger Support for Our DApp
    Ledger users, we heard you! You can now use your Ledger device to sign transactions directly in our DApp. This brings a big boost to both security and usability, making it easier to manage your BZE assets with confidence.
  • Automated Coin Burning from Trading Fees
    Our burner module just got smarter. Instead of requiring a governance proposal every time we want to burn coins from trading fees, the process is now fully automated. Coins are burned every 4 weeks, helping maintain long-term value and keeping the protocol lean — no manual steps needed.

This upgrade marks a big step forward in making BZE more efficient and user-friendly.

🛠️ Our DApp Keeps Evolving

Our DApp is the main hub for everything BZE — from trading on the DEX to staking rewards and more. We’re continuously working on improving it, adding new features, and making the overall experience smoother for everyone.

On top of that, the POSTHUMAN Validator Team is currently working on a full UI redesign. So, in the coming months, you can expect a fresh new look and an even more intuitive interface. The best version of the BZE DApp is still to come.

🗺️ 2025 Roadmap & What We’re Building Right Now

Our 2025 roadmap is live on the website! It outlines our key goals and major updates planned for this year, giving everyone a clear view of what’s ahead.

That said, not everything we’re working on is listed there. Some initiatives are still in early exploration or happening behind the scenes — and if they come to life, they’ll be announced when the time is right. Just know that the roadmap is a guide, not a limit.

As for what’s happening right now — we’ve moved past the planning phase and are actively building the next network upgrade. This release will bring:

  • AMM liquidity pools to our DEX
  • A Cosmos SDK upgrade
  • Other important features & improvements

Development is in full swing, and we’re targeting a mainnet launch in April. More details will be shared as we get closer!

🧱 Max Supply Cap: 400 Million BZE

Following a recent governance proposal, the BZE community has officially decided to set a maximum supply cap of 400 million BZE — a major milestone in defining the future of our tokenomics.

Right now, around 13–14 million BZE are minted each year, and the current total supply is about 261 millions. So while we’re still many years away from reaching the 400M cap, this mechanism will be implemented this year to ensure the blockchain fully enforces the community’s decision.

Here’s how it will work:
When the supply hits 400 million, the blockchain will automatically set inflation to 0, stopping any further minting.

Since BZE has a built-in burning mechanism, the total supply can decrease over time. If enough coins are burned and the supply falls back below 400M, minting can resume — but only if the community approves it via a governance-controlled parameter.

This ensures that the max supply isn’t just a guideline — it’s enforced on-chain and shaped by the community.

🎉 BZE Turns 3 — Thank You for Being Part of the Journey!

Today is a special day for us — it’s BZE’s 3rd birthday! Our very first block was produced on March 21, 2022 at 22:39 UTC, and it’s amazing to see how far we’ve come since then.

Three years ago, we made a big move: we migrated from our original blockchain to the Cosmos SDK. Like any big transition, the beginning was a bit slow — we had to adjust, lay down new foundations, and rebuild some core pieces.

But now, things are moving faster. We’re shipping new features more often, improving the chain, and opening up new possibilities — all thanks to the continued support of our community.

item.title: Let’s Take a Moment to Enjoy What We Achieved in 2024
item.dc:creator: beezee
item.content:encoded:
As we step into 2025, it’s the perfect moment to reflect on the extraordinary progress we made in 2024. This past year was pivotal for BZE, as we turned ambitious goals into tangible achievements, strengthened our ecosystem, and set the stage for future growth.

From blockchain upgrades to innovative dApp features, from mobile developments to strategic partnerships, 2024 was about laying a foundation that empowers our community and opens doors to exciting opportunities. Here’s a look back at the milestones we reached and a glimpse into what lies ahead.

Key Achievements of 2024

1. Launching and Upgrading Core Infrastructure

  • BZE Blockchain: v7 Upgrade
    This transformative upgrade introduced the Token Factory, Rewards, and an integrated DEX, enabling users to manage assets seamlessly and trade efficiently within the BZE ecosystem.
  • BZE Blockchain: v7.1 Upgrade
    Building on v7, this release brought Burning Raffles and further DEX enhancements, demonstrating our commitment to innovation and community engagement.

2. Expanding the BZE dApp Ecosystem

  • Initial dApp Release
    We launched the first version of the BZE dApp, featuring Token Factory, Rewards, and the Burner, giving users powerful tools for managing and utilizing their assets.
  • DEX Enhancements
    Throughout the year, we added DEX Trading, a DEX Aggregator & API, and secured listings on CoinGecko and LiveCoinWatch, expanding access and visibility for our decentralized exchange.
  • Burning Raffles
    This unique feature gamified the burning process, encouraging community participation while reducing token supply.

3. CoinTrunk.io: A Gateway to Mobile Crypto Experiences

2024 saw the release of the CoinTrunk.io Mobile App for Android, providing users with a streamlined, on-the-go experience for managing crypto assets. With a solid foundation in place, we’re committed to continuous improvements to ensure CoinTrunk.io becomes a must-have tool for mobile-first users.

4. Strengthening the Ecosystem: A Home for Projects

BZE is rapidly becoming a reliable hub for crypto projects.

  • VDL Migration
    We successfully facilitated the migration of VDL from its native chain to BZE, highlighting the security and reliability of our blockchain.
  • Staking Rewards for SHERPA
    As a gift to the Sherpa Coin community, we introduced a staking rewards program where users can earn incentives for staking their tokens on the BZE network.

5. Revamped Website

To better communicate our mission and progress, we launched a redesigned BZE Website. This update offers a clearer explanation of our work and serves as a resource for both newcomers and long-time supporters.

29M $BZE Burned: A Deflationary Milestone

In 2024, we executed a major burning event, permanently removing 29M $BZE from circulation. But that was just the beginning. With our dApp and DEX now live, we’re consistently capturing and redirecting fees to the burner module and the community pool. Here’s how:

  • DEX Market Pairs: We’ve created 7 market pairs, contributing 25K $BZE per pair to the community pool.
  • Staking Rewards: Two staking reward programs have launched, each contributing 25K $BZE to the community pool.
  • Trading Fees: All the DEX trade fees — some of the lowest in the market — are set at just 0.1 BZE for market takers (approximately $0.00008938 USD) and 0.001 BZE for market makers (approximately $0.0000008938 USD) based on the current BZE coin value of $0.0008938 USD as listed on CoinGecko at the time of this writing. These fees are directly sent to the burner module, contributing to the deflationary mechanism of the BZE ecosystem.

Why split the fees? Flexibility. Funds in the community pool can either be burned or repurposed to meet the network’s needs — ensuring we strike the right balance between deflationary measures and strategic growth.

Looking Ahead to 2025

While we’re proud of what we’ve achieved, the journey doesn’t stop here. The 2025 roadmap will be unveiled in the coming days, packed with opportunities for BZE holders and newcomers alike. Stay tuned — it’s a vision you won’t want to miss.
